study_plan.title: Make borrow atomic
study_plan.action: Rewrite borrow_book to perform a single UPDATE with a WHERE clause checking availability, verify rowcount, and return appropriate response.

study_plan.title: Add transaction handling
study_plan.action: Wrap the SELECT, UPDATE, and INSERT statements in a BEGIN...COMMIT transaction using a context manager and ensure connections are closed after each request.

study_plan.title: Secure JWT flow
study_plan.action: Document the JWT verification process in get_current_user, add error handling, and create a unit test that decodes a token and checks the returned user dict.

study_plan.title: Upgrade password hashing
study_plan.action: Replace hash_password with pass‑lib's bcrypt/argon2 implementation, store per‑user salts, and move SECRET_KEY to an environment variable via python‑dotenv.

study_plan.title: Concurrency test suite
study_plan.action: Write a pytest using threading or async client to issue concurrent borrow requests for the same copy and assert only one succeeds, confirming race‑condition safety.

recruiter_summary: The student understands the insecurity of an unsalted SHA‑256 password hash and can articulate why a dedicated hashing library is preferable. They recognize SQLite's single‑writer limitation but cannot explain transaction handling, atomicity, or crash behavior. Their explanation of JWT verification and the borrow concurrency safeguards is absent, and the existing tests do not simulate real concurrent requests. Overall, the candidate demonstrates partial technical knowledge but needs significant improvement in secure authentication, database transaction management, and race‑condition mitigation.
